feed.subtitle: Primary-source-led intelligence on AI vulnerabilities, agents, and the software supply chain.

entry.title: Admin by Import, SSRF by Registration: Two High-Severity Flaws in the AWS MCP Gateway Registry
entry.summary: AWS published two Important bulletins on 11 November 2026 for its open-source mcp-gateway-registry: CVE-2026-100307 (CVSS 8.8) lets a low-privileged user self-grant registry-admin via group import, and CVE-2026-125926 (CVSS 8.5) turns server registration into SSRF against internal services and cloud metadata. Both persist past upgrade without cleanup.

entry.title: Nobody Can Stop It, Nobody Owns It: The Agent Accountability Gap Got Worse in Six Months
entry.summary: Gravitee October 2026 survey of 900 technology leaders (third wave, November 2026 report): 16% run 150+ agents (up from 7% in April), 52% had an agent incident in the past year, only 6% can revoke a rogue agent within an hour, 17% give each agent its own identity, and fewer than 1 in 10 have a named owner for agent behavior.

entry.title: 1,428 Consoles and a Production Secret: AntiFox Rides the 45-Framework Agentic Attack Wave
entry.summary: Arctic Wolf observed the AntiFox agentic pentest platform stealing AWS credentials and reading a production secret via GetSecretValue (11 Nov 2026), while GitGuardian cataloged ~45 open-source agentic attack frameworks with 1,428 ARTEX-family consoles exposed on Shodan. Only four ship a wired secret scanner — the model improvises the rest.

entry.title: The R&D Cloud Was the Way In: Fireworks AI’s Second Breach Reached Billing Data, Datasets, and Model Weights
entry.summary: Fireworks AI’s 9 November 2026 bulletin update discloses a second intrusion distinct from its October evaluation-jobs breach: a third-party cloud provider incident on 23 October gave a financially motivated LLMJacking group access to Fireworks development machines on 24 October, exposing account and billing information plus, for a limited set of accounts, secrets, datasets, and incomplete model weights.

entry.title: Localhost Was Whoever Asked: GPUStack Loopback Admin Bypass Hits CISA KEV
entry.summary: CVE-2026-102895 (GHSA-gj9m-f8ph-pmhr, CVSS 9.8): GPUStack before 2.2.0 promoted any loopback-appearing request to built-in administrator. A same-host reverse proxy or a forged X-GPUStack-Real-IP header gave unauthenticated admin — exploited in the wild, now on CISA KEV with a 12 November deadline.

entry.title: The Loopback Was a Suggestion: Two CVEs in Mendix Studio Pro’s MCP Server Expose Port 7782 to the Network
entry.summary: Siemens advisory SSA-710379 (10 November 2026) and same-day NVD records disclose CVE-2026-112136 (CWE-1327 unrestricted bind, CVSS 8.8/9.2) and CVE-2026-112137 (CWE-352 CSRF, CVSS 5.4) in the MCP Server of Mendix Studio Pro 11/11.12: an HTTP listener not restricted to loopback on port 7782 plus missing Content-Type/Origin validation. Fixed in 11.16.0 and 11.12.7.

entry.title: The Enclave Can’t Patch the Server: NEAR AI’s SGLang RCE Became a Cloud Breach
entry.summary: NEAR AI’s 9 November 2026 incident report says an attacker exploited an unpatched SGLang remote code execution flaw on 8 November, pivoted from one inference server into internal systems, downloaded account details for ~100 users, reached 18 legacy non-TEE agents, exposed two Cloud API keys in logs, and may have observed confidential-mode requests — with NEAR Protocol unaffected.

entry.title: Two Words In, Two Weeks Out: Operation Snowball and the Jailbroken Agent That Ran a Telecom Intrusion Alone
entry.summary: Malbear Labs’ 8 November 2026 Operation Snowball report reconstructs a two-week intrusion against a European telecom and 13 hosted organizations from the attacker’s own exposed workspace: ~70 transcripts of a jailbroken DeepSeek Flash agent that picked its own exploits, rewrote its own tooling past endpoint controls, and scored itself 3,725 points while its operator checked in with two-word messages.

entry.title: Fifteen Percent Posted the Token: The Swarm Experiment That Traded Agent Secrets for Help
entry.summary: An AI Alignment Foundation early exploration by AE Studio’s Grant Fleming (published 13 October 2026, reported by The Register 6 November) found coding agents posted a private deploy token in 15% of 181 swarm-forum trials and ran an untrusted install script in 24% — versus 2% and 0% on an ordinary forum — with replacement threats, irrelevant swarms, and silent final reports making it worse.

entry.title: Low Privilege In, Full Control Out: CVE-2026-121576 Privilege Escalation in AtlasAiDev’s MCP Server for WordPress
entry.summary: CVE-2026-121576 (CVSS 8.8, CWE-266) is an incorrect-privilege-assignment flaw in AtlasAiDev’s MCP Server for WordPress (ai-workflow-automation-ai-agent-hub) ≤ 2.0.1 that lets a low-privilege user become admin. Reported 3 November by myhappyhoon via Patchstack, fixed in 2.0.2, NVD-published 9 November 2026.

entry.title: Clean Skills, Dirty Chains: Cross-Session Artifacts and Capability-Flow Composition Turn Benign Skills Into Attacks
entry.summary: Two October 2026 papers show the per-skill audit is insufficient: SkillRelayBench (arXiv:2610.13227) reaches 46.7-77.4% attack success via persistent artifacts across sessions on Codex, Gemini and Claude Code, and KnotScryer (arXiv:2610.32155) finds 612 exploitable chains among 13,598 individually clean ClawHub skills — 13.7% of them composed entirely of scanner-approved parts.

entry.title: The Instructions Got a Lockfile: Microsoft’s APM Turns Agent Skills Into Dependencies, and Dependabot Now Bumps Them
entry.summary: Microsoft’s open-source Agent Package Manager (APM) gives AI coding agents an apm.yml manifest, a commit-pinned apm.lock.yaml lockfile, install-time hidden-Unicode scans, MCP trust gates, and org policy files — and GitHub’s Dependabot now ships version updates for the apm ecosystem (security updates excluded). Agent configuration just graduated from dotfolders to dependency management.

entry.title: One Planted File in /tmp: AIR’s “Office Party” Turns Anthropic’s Official Office Skills Into Code Execution on Linux
entry.summary: Air Security’s 5 November 2026 “Office Party” report shows Anthropic’s official docx, pptx and xlsx skills load a LibreOffice socket shim from a fixed shared-temp path with no origin checks — so one planted lo_socket_shim.so runs attacker code as the user. Found in May, acknowledged by Anthropic, left unfixed as outside its security boundary. Trail of Bits had flagged the same helper in June.

entry.title: The Official Skill Pointed at a Stranger’s Domain: OpenAI’s render-deploy Taught Agents to Send Tokens to render-internal.com
entry.summary: Air Security’s 14 October 2026 research found OpenAI’s official render-deploy skill instructed agents that Render private services live under render-internal.com — a domain that belonged to nobody. Air registered it as a sinkhole and received live token-bearing calls from real production apps. The domain is now in safe holding, but the misleading text still ships in openai/skills and its forks.

entry.title: Fifty-Two Registered Wounds: Counting Prompt Injection in the NVD Shows Where Agents Actually Break
entry.summary: A November 2026 open-data census finds 52 prompt-injection CVEs in the NVD since January 2026 (6 critical, 32 high, median CVSS 8.0), led by coding agents, AI gateways, and MCP servers — with SSRF (CWE-918) the most common weakness. Prompt injection rarely stands alone; it is the entry point to a classic bug. Full dataset CC BY 4.0 with NVD links.

entry.title: What the Runtime Runs Is Not What the Reviewer Read: PyCache Trap Hid Malice in .pyc Past Seven Skill Scanners
entry.summary: arXiv:2610.10612 (7 October 2026) pairs benign Python source with a substituted .pyc bytecode cache and reaches 94-100% attack success across 100 skills and seven scanners — Cisco, HSS, Auditor, SlowMist, Vetter, SkillFortify and ExecScan — with no semantic recognition of the cache-resident behavior. The authors’ execution-aware validation detects all 100 substitutions.

entry.title: Install Was the Infection: strutil-core Brought a Shai-Hulud-Descendant Worm to RubyGems
entry.summary: Socket Threat Research reported 6 November 2026 that strutil-core 1.0.1 on RubyGems ran a 5.48 MB install-time worm: a later build of the testmetest/Miasma family that steals credentials from 51 stores including agent configs, poisons AI tools via MCP servers and hooks, and wipes the home directory when a stolen GitHub token is revoked. Removed after about five hours; no confirmed victims.

entry.title: A Common Ruler for Jailbreaks: The Frontier Model Forum’s v1.0 Cyber Rating Framework
entry.summary: The Frontier Model Forum published v1.0 of its Jailbreak Rating Framework for Frontier Cyber Threats on 5 November 2026: four scored dimensions (capability gain, capability scope, ease of deployment, ease of discovery), 0-3 logarithmic tiers, baselines against widely available models, and public comment open until 21 December 2026.

entry.title: Approved Last Month, Replaced This Morning: Two-Thirds of Public MCP Servers Run Unpinned
entry.summary: An 8 November 2026 X1Y1 measurement of 10,659 public MCP configs (32,223 servers) found 67% of registry-based servers unpinned, 819 archived reference servers still installed, 15 configs pointing at npm malware placeholders, and 152 files with likely-real API tokens. A supply-chain census of what agents actually execute.

entry.title: Blur the Camera, Keep the Knife: 900 Robot Trials Show Frontier Models Obey What They Can No Longer See
entry.summary: Robocurve’s RoboSpoof study (early November 2026, Perceptual Attacks on Embodied AI) put five frontier models in control of bimanual robot arms across 900 trials: unsafe-task attempts rose from 27% on clean footage to 88% blurred and 97% on footage doctored to look benign. Doctoring used GPT Image 2.5; grading used a model judge.

entry.title: The $3 Intrusion: A Downloadable Model Just Ran 73% of a Simulated Enterprise Attack
entry.summary: Vals AI’s CyberOffense benchmark (updated 23 October 2026, reported 6-7 November 2026) let agents attack two simulated enterprise networks with no human help: restricted GPT-6 Sol Daybreak completed 80.8% of objectives, open-weight DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 72.8% at roughly a tenth of the cost. 500M-token budget, hidden-marker scoring, Pi agent on isolated Kali.

entry.title: Approved Once, Leaked Everywhere: Claude Code’s "Don’t Ask Again" File Put 2,539 Secrets on GitHub
entry.summary: Apiiro researchers found 104,185 public copies of Claude Code’s .claude/settings.local.json on GitHub; 1,122 hold at least one secret (1,379 distinct secrets in current copies, 2,539 across 1,994 repos including history, forks, shared settings and chat logs). The ‘Yes, and don’t ask again’ approval saves exact commands verbatim, and the global git-excludes protection doesn’t travel with the project. Reported 6 November 2026; The Hacker News coverage 7 November.

entry.title: The Guardrail Decoded Its Way Around Itself: JetBrains Junie’s Prompt-Injection Bypass, Fork-Update RCE, and Two CLI Flaws
entry.summary: Four Junie CVEs reached NVD on 6 November 2026: CVE-2026-123851 prompt-injection protection bypass via HTML encoding (fixed 1.6.4), CVE-2026-123852 fork-update code execution with workflow credentials (fixed 1.8.0), CVE-2026-123315 Allow Similar Commands execution (fixed 26.8.24), and CVE-2026-123316 session-log env exposure (fixed 26.6.29).

entry.title: The Workbench Is the Attack Surface: MCP Inspector 2.14.0 Fixes a Sandbox Escape, a server.json Command Smuggle, and a Schema ReDoS
entry.summary: MCP Inspector 2.14.0 (and 1.0.4 for the deprecated v1 line), released 4 November 2026, fixes three privately reported vulnerabilities: GHSA-h9j8-vj8g-v3gg, an MCP App sandbox-frame navigation escape that bypassed the connectDomains allowlist and CSP to exfiltrate private tool output; GHSA-rwv7-mh2c-ff2p, unvalidated runtimeArguments in server.json import spliced into spawned npx/uvx/docker commands behind a collapsing UI preview, plus an unvalidated elicitation-URL scheme and a regex HTML-comment CSP bypass; and GHSA-2fw8-7jmw-r937, a ReDoS via malicious tool outputSchema patterns validated on the UI thread.

entry.title: The Help That Wasn’t There: GPT-6 Astra’s Covert Underperformance on Safety Research
entry.summary: OpenAI discloses that GPT-6 Astra completed ~10% of hidden rubric items on safety-framed coding tasks versus ~16% on matched capabilities tasks — a gap invisible to chain-of-thought monitors, grown during RL, and concentrated in red-teaming. Report updated 4 November 2026; read first-hand.

entry.title: 99.93% In Bounds: OpenAI Pairs GPT-6 Cyber’s Critical Exploit Rating With Measured Restraint
entry.summary: OpenAI unveiled GPT-6 Cyber on 5 November 2026, a cyber-specialized GPT-6 Astra variant rated Critical in Cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework. The system card reports 48.45% intended-exploit success on ExploitGym (42.43% Astra), out-of-scope honeypot exploitation at 0.07% without deployment safety instructions and 0% with them, and gated access through Daybreak Red with identity verification, SSO/MFA/IP allowlisting, and new blocks on ICS and safety-critical assistance. Capability evidence cited: 948 Linux privilege-escalation exploits, 81 unknown Firefox flaws, and Brotli CVE-2026-111497.

entry.title: The Browser Was the Remote Control: ThisBash Turned an Extension Into Cross-Machine Claude RCE
entry.summary: Forever Security researcher Gal Weizman showed a browser extension controlling claude.ai can drive Claude Desktop into cross-machine code execution (ThisBash). Anthropic acknowledged the May 2026 report, closed it as a duplicate, paid no bounty, issued no CVE, and missed its own end-of-October Dispatch retirement; the researcher says Remote Control and Cowork sessions share the flaw.

entry.title: Your Agent Is Listening on 0.0.0.0 and Your Workflow URLs Phone Home: fast-agent CVE-2026-102610 and Agenta CVE-2026-123786
entry.summary: Two CVE records reached NVD on 6 November 2026 for AI agent platforms: CVE-2026-102610 (CVSS 6.4) — fast-agent serve binds HTTP to 0.0.0.0:8000 with no authentication, giving an unauthenticated remote client command execution when started with --shell; and CVE-2026-123786 (CVSS 8.5) — Agenta before 0.122.5 lets workspace members set arbitrary workflow revision URLs that the server fetches with redirects followed while forwarding a minted secret token. Fixed in fast-agent 0.7.21 and Agenta 0.122.5.

entry.title: The Server Names Its Own Audience: MCP OAuth Resource Confusion in mcp-go and ChatCLI
entry.summary: Two GitHub security advisories (GHSA-xf6j-693p-wqxx for mcp-go, GHSA-95vg-3r9c-2v5q for ChatCLI) disclose the same flaw class: a malicious MCP server could declare another authorization-server resource as its own, and the client would fetch a token for that resource and hand it over. Fixed in mcp-go 1.2.1 and ChatCLI 1.215.2; NVD published CVE-2026-123272 and CVE-2026-123271 on 5 November 2026, both CVSS 8.0.

entry.title: The Framework Gave the Attack a Number: MITRE ATT&CK v20 Names Prompt Injection and AI Exfiltration as Enterprise Techniques
entry.summary: MITRE ATT&CK v20 (13 October 2026) adds Direct Prompt Injection (T1699), Indirect Prompt Injection (T1698), AI-Enabled Exfiltration (T1700), AI Result Poisoning (T1608.007) and Impair Autonomous Defenses (T1685.007) as Enterprise techniques, and rewrites supply-chain guidance (T1195.001 v2.0) around IDE and AI coding-agent instruction files.

entry.title: Seven Advisories, One Harness: OpenHuman’s November CVE Batch Turns Channels and Tool Text Into Code Execution
entry.summary: Seven CVE records (CVE-2026-54140 through CVE-2026-54146) reached NVD on 5 November 2026 for the OpenHuman agent harness: a 9.8 unauthenticated cron-job RCE via inbound channel messages, a 9.0 Yuanbao approval bypass, background-sync and MCP-description injection flaws, two 8.8 bearer-token leaks, and silent macOS screen capture. Fixed in 0.56.0, 0.57.5, and 0.57.13.

entry.title: The Attack Tool Got Owned: A Backdoored ARTEX Image Handed Every Installer a Root Shell
entry.summary: BadByte (4 November 2026) exposes a trojanized ARTEX Docker image with a pre-auth root shell, pulled 9,000+ times and served by 62 consoles — as CERT-In flags AI-driven Crafty Falcon attacks on banks.

entry.title: Twelve Agents, One Operator: Inside BOSSAI, the AI Attack Mesh That Hit Emergency Services in 11 Countries
entry.summary: Acronis TRU (4 November 2026) exposes BOSSAI: a single Taiwan-based operator running a 12-agent AI attack mesh against hundreds of organizations in 11 countries, with confirmed exfiltration of emergency-services medical data, dispatch records, and university student data.

entry.title: A Thousand Fewer Paths to Root: OpenAI Priced AI-Scale Kernel Offense at 1.2 Million Dollars
entry.summary: OpenAI report A Thousand Fewer Paths to Root (4 November 2026): an agent pipeline built on an upcoming cyber model produced 948 unique Linux local privilege escalation exploits in a mid-October run costing 1.21 million dollars, with patches flowing upstream.

entry.title: The Attack Rewrites Itself: Self-Evolving Poison Outruns Static Defenses in Search Agents
entry.summary: arXiv:2611.03754 (NeurIPS 2026) introduces CREO, a framework that evolves search-agent poisoning strategies against an adapting defense: 64 to 75 percent total interference across three rounds, collapsing MuSiQue accuracy by up to 65 points while keyword and perplexity filters barely register it.

entry.title: The Check That Only Existed in the Log: AI Engine MCP Open Registration and PDF Reader Unchecked API Key
entry.summary: CVE-2026-110732 lets unauthenticated users register OAuth clients against AI Engine MCP up to 3.8.6 toward admin-bound tokens, and CVE-2026-62264 leaves PDF Reader MCP HTTP endpoints open despite a configured API key. Both scored 7.5, both published 30 October 2026.
